extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and policymakers interested in American federalism, parties, and press liberty
extracted.subtask_description: Expository chapter-length analysis of the durability and weaknesses of federal systems, the dynamics of political parties, popular sovereignty, and the liberty of the press in the United States. Aimed at explaining causal conditions and characteristic behaviors rather than giving procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inducements_to_union_for_durability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal compact cannot be lasting unless there exists in the communities which are leagued together a certain number of inducements to union which render their common dependence agreeable, and the task of the Government light, and that system cannot succeed without the presence of favorable circumstances added to the influence of good laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common interests, favorable circumstances, and the influence of good laws are necessary intellectual ties of association for any confederation; mere legal devices cannot by themselves prevent dangerous collisions between sovereignties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity_of_civilization_needed
rubrics_metrics.description: A certain uniformity of civilization is not less necessary to the durability of a confederation than a uniformity of interests in the States which compose it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If constituent units differ widely in civilization (example: Canton of Uri vs. Vaud), a central authority prescribing uniform laws will fail; practical uniformity across regions makes a federal system feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common_origin_and_language_as_bonds
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the circumstances which most powerfully contribute to support the Federal Government in America is that the States have not only similar interests, a common origin, and a common tongue, but that they are also arrived at the same stage of civilization;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shared origin, language, and stage of civilization strengthen inducements to union and make federal government more practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical_position_as_safeguard
rubrics_metrics.description: The great advantage of the United States does not, then, consist in a Federal Constitution which allows them to carry on great wars, but in a geographical position which renders such enterprises extremely improbable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insulation by geography (vast continent, sparse hostile neighbors) reduces likelihood of great wars, which in turn helps preserve a federal system that would otherwise be vulnerable in prolonged conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: War_weakens_federal_governments
rubrics_metrics.description: A long war almost always places nations in the wretched alternative of being abandoned to ruin by defeat or to despotism by success. War therefore renders the symptoms of the weakness of a government most palpable and most alarming; and I have shown that the inherent defeat of federal governments is that of being weak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal systems, being inherently weaker in centralized administration, struggle to conduct prolonged, large-scale wars and are prone either to collapse or to centralization/despotism when faced with such wars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deficiencies_of_centralized_administration_in_federations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal system is not only deficient in every kind of centralized administration, but the central government itself is imperfectly organized, which is invariably an influential cause of inferiority when the nation is opposed to other countries which are themselves governed by a single authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples (militia command disputes) show that ambiguity of federal vs state authority and decentralized organization impede effective national responses and weaken the union.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical_limits_of_legal_fictions_between_sovereignties
rubrics_metrics.description: He would have but a partial knowledge of the world who should imagine that it is possible, by the aid of legal fictions, to prevent men from finding out and employing those means of gratifying their passions which have been left open to them;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal fictions cannot mask real conflicts of interest between state and federal authorities; litigation framed as private suits masks de facto interstate conflicts that law alone may not resolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: People_as_real_directing_power_under_representative_forms
rubrics_metrics.description: In America the people appoints the legislative and the executive power, and furnishes the jurors who punish all offences against the laws... The people is therefore the real directing power; and although the form of government is representative, it is evident that the opinions, the prejudices, the interests, and even the passions of the community are hindered by no durable obstacles from exercising a perpetual influence on society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent, direct elections and jury service render representatives dependent on popular opinion; majority rule and party agitation keep the people as the active governing force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction_between_great_and_minor_parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The political parties which I style great are those which cling to principles more than to their consequences... Minor parties are, on the other hand, generally deficient in political faith. As they are not sustained or dignified by a lofty purpose, they ostensibly display the egotism of their character in their actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great parties: principled, broader ideas, nobler passions; Minor parties: interest-driven, factitious zeal, timid and irresolute conduct; these differences affect the character and impact of party politics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes_and_formation_of_parties
rubrics_metrics.description: A political aspirant in the United States begins by discriminating his own interest, and by calculating upon those interests which may be collected around and amalgamated with it; he then contrives to discover some doctrine or some principle which may suit the purposes of this new association, and which he adopts in order to bring forward his party and to secure his popularity;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are manufactured by political actors aggregating interests and adopting doctrines as rallying cries; creation of parties is an art of coalition-building rather than spontaneous emergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence_of_great_parties_leads_to_many_minor_controversies
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of great parties, the United States abound with lesser controversies; and public opinion is divided into a thousand minute shades of difference upon questions of very little moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When grand ideological cleavages are absent, political life fragments into numerous small disputes and finely graded public-opinion divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior_of_wealthy_classes_under_democratic_preponderance
rubrics_metrics.description: The more affluent classes of society are so entirely removed from the direction of political affairs in the United States that wealth, far from conferring a right to the exercise of power, is rather an obstacle than a means of attaining to it. The wealthy members of the community abandon the lists... They concentrate all their enjoyments in the privacy of their homes...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wealthy individuals often retreat from public contest, cultivate private exclusivity, and adopt public deference; this constitutes a private aristocracy of manners despite democratic institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary_weapons_of_parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The two chief weapons which parties use in order to ensure success are the public press and the formation of associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organized associations and control/influence of the press are the main instruments by which parties mobilize support and shape public opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberty_of_the_press_as_correlative_of_popular_sovereignty
rubrics_metrics.description: The sovereignty of the people and the liberty of the press may therefore be looked upon as correlative institutions; just as the censorship of the press and universal suffrage are two things which are irreconcilably opposed, and which cannot long be retained among the institutions of the same people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a polity where citizens are presumed capable of discriminating opinions, censorship is both dangerous and absurd; free press and popular rule mutually sustain each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits_and_dangers_of_repressing_press_abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is your intention to correct the abuses of unlicensed printing and to restore the use of orderly language, you may in the first instance try the offender by a jury... If you establish a censorship of the press, the tongue of the public speaker will still make itself heard, and you have only increased the mischief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial prosecution may diffuse and amplify censored ideas; censorship often fails and can slide toward despotism; opening restrictions can paradoxically spread the censored views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press_as_independent_of_social_conditions_in_its_vehemence
rubrics_metrics.description: The periodical press appears to me to be actuated by passions and propensities independent of the circumstances in which it is placed... America is perhaps, at this moment, the country of the whole world which contains the fewest germs of revolution; but the press is not less destructive in its principles than in France, and it displays the same violence without the same reasons for indignation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tone and violence of the press may stem from internal propensities of the periodical press rather than directly from objective social grievances; thus tempering social conditions alone may not moderate press vehemence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press_as_sole_guarantee_where_legal_redress_absent
rubrics_metrics.description: For in certain countries which profess to enjoy the privileges of freedom every individual agent of the Government may violate the laws with impunity, since those whom he oppresses cannot prosecute him before the courts of justice. In this case the liberty of the press is not merely a guarantee, but it is the only guarantee, of their liberty and their security which the citizens possess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where ordinary legal remedies against government agents are unavailable, a free press functions as an essential public check and watchdog; eliminating it would remove citizens' only effective redress.
